messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a seq-length profiling sweep against prod routes this morning, and saw a consistent tail on routes with long prompt prefixes. CPU/GPU kernel selection keeps flipping for tokens > 1k and we're hitting much higher p95 token time than expected. :thinking:
ken: can you paste the profiling trace? is this kernel selection (cu kernels) or batching heuristic thrash?
maria: attached flame in the dashboard, but TL;DR: runtime chose the small-kernel path for the attention op mid-sequence which forces a slow memcpy path. stack trace snippet:
```
runtime: select_kernel(attn, seq_len=1208) -> kernel_small
kernel_small: optimized for <=1024 seq, fallback memcpy, 2x latency
config: batching_policy=dynamic_auto, kv_cache_enabled=true
```
jess: oh, small-kernel mispick. we've seen heuristics based on avg seq length per worker. dynamic_auto probably uses the running mean which gets polluted by short bursts.
liam: question — is the KV cache staleness causing different memory layout so select_kernel gets different heuristic inputs?
maria: yes. when KV cache slices are fragmented (after many different routes), the runtime reports a lower contiguous token window to the selector. that nudges kernel choice. I have a quick repro script that toggles route diversity and shows selector flip.
ops-bot: [deploy] perf-probe-v2 started for slice: us-west-2 - job id 6789
ken: nice. any visible correlation on per-route token breakdown graphs? p50/p95/p99 per-token?
maria: updated the token timeline dashboard: /dashboards/runtime/token_timeline?route=chat-heavy — shows token-level latency lines where tokens 800-1250 spike. p99 jumps from 120ms->420ms.
jess: suggestion: change selection to consider contiguous kv-window size and prefer kernel_large if contiguous_window >= 1024 even if mean seq < 1024. Also add a 5s stabilizer to avoid flip-flopping.
liam: that plus adjusting batching heuristic threshold (min_batch_size ramp) should reduce tail. we can also add a metric: kernel_selection_flip_rate per worker.
maria: I already added a counter metric: runtime.kernel.selector.flips -> exposed in telemetry, emits tags: worker_id, route, kv_contig_size. visible in the new per-route KPIs.
sre-oncall: important for alerting — how do we want to surface this in SLOs? current latency burn alerts trigger too late; paging threshold at burnrate=3+ for 15m. We need a pre-page signal.
ken: propose: add anomaly detector on kernel_selection_flip_rate and token_p99_derivative. If flip_rate spikes > 10/min AND token_p99 derivative > 2x in 5m window -> raise warning channel (not page) with runbook link. If persistent 20m -> page.
jm note: runbook link -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-flip
jess: also add a dashboard panel: per-worker flip heatmap + top offending routes, with quick action buttons: disable-dyn-auto for that worker or force kernel_large.
liam: can we ship an automated canary: when flips detected, temporarily pin kernel to large for 10min and measure p99 delta, then auto-revert. that will give A/B data. needs rollout policy though.
sre-oncall: agree on staged approach. implement metric + warning alert first. paging only if warning persists. update SLO doc after we have baseline.
maria: I'll push the metric PR and the dashboard patch. will also attach the repro script in the PR. expecting to have data in staging in ~2 hours.
ken: thanks — once PR is up drop link here and tag me. also add unit tests for selector decision boundary. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [ci] pipeline #342 succeeded for branch: runtime/kernel-flip-metrics
maria: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/409 — includes metric + dashboard JSON + repro steps. collecting staging traces now.
sre-oncall: noted. I'll add a warning alert to the ops channel with the suggested thresholds (flip_rate > 10/min + token_p99_deriv > 2x). we'll iterate on thresholds after staging data. :eyes:
